Subject: RFP Q14: evidence retainability & extractability — SOW request

Elliot,

Thanks for the quick engagement so far. As part of our procurement due diligence for RFP STR-2027-045, Legal has asked for a concise SOW / technical appendix that addresses our requirements for audit trail retainability and exportability (RFP Q14). Specifically they want the following clarified: 

- Default retention windows for audit trails and admin logs (standard tiers + enterprise commitments)
- Supported export formats and a sample export manifest (file-level metadata, checksums, schema)
- Chain-of-custody / tamper evidence mechanisms and timestamp provenance
- Redaction/pseudonymization options for PII in extracts and whether redaction affects audit fidelity
- Delivery options for evidence packages (S3 presigned, cross-account S3, bulk transfer) and typical delivery SLAs
- Any contractual controls (SLA/credits) around bulk evidence delivery

Can you provide: (1) a short SOW + appendix we can attach to the RFP response, and (2) a sample manifest we can show Security (they prefer an NDJSON example)? Due date for our pack is 2027-10-10.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m call if helpful.

Best,
Mina Khurana

Mina — thanks for the detail and the deadline. We can provide both a short SOW appendix and an NDJSON sample manifest. I attached a one-page export-spec summary and a sample_extract_manifest JSON to this email for immediate review.

High level answers:
- Retention: default platform audit trails retained 90 days; enterprise customers can elect 1 / 3 / 7 year windows via contract.
- Export formats: NDJSON, Parquet, gzipped bundles; manifest includes file-level SHA256 checksums and record counts.
- Tamper evidence: manifests are signed by Redwood using an HSM-backed key and include a monotonic timestamp chain; we provide checksums and optional signed ledger entries for long-term retention.
- Delivery: presigned cross-account S3 is standard (48–72 hour delivery SLA for typical packages). Physical media by exception and under SOW.

I looped in Ben to coordinate procurement language and Laura for the technical appendix. Would you like a brief call tomorrow morning to walk Security through the manifest?

Thanks,
Elliot
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RFP Q14: evidence retainability & extractability — technical appendix (export mechanics)

Mina / team — technical appendix notes below; I’ve kept this concise for the RFP appendix but happy to expand for your Security ops.

Export mechanics (summary):
- Formats: NDJSON (line-delimited JSON), Apache Parquet (columnar), and gzipped tarballs for bulk movement. Each export bundle includes a top-level manifest (manifest.ndjson) and per-file metadata.
- Manifest schema (attached sample_extract_manifest.json): each manifest entry includes {filename, record_count, first_event_ts, last_event_ts, sha256_hex, file_size_bytes, table_name, record_schema_id}. We provide schema IDs that map to a stable schema registry we host for the customer.
- Checksums & signature: each file includes a SHA256 checksum. The manifest itself is signed using an HSM-backed RSA key (PKCS#11); signature block and signer key id are included in the manifest metadata. For customers requiring ledgered proof, we offer an optional append-only signing ledger (Merkle-tree anchoring) with timestamp provenance and inclusion proofs.
- Timestamp provenance & monotonicity: export items use event timestamps (UTC, RFC3339) derived from our system clock; for tamper evidence the manifest includes both event_timestamp and export_timestamp and a monotonic export_sequence number.
- Retention windows: default 90 days for admin/audit logs. Enterprise tier offers contractable retention tiers: 1 year, 3 years, or 7 years (long-term retention archived to cold storage). Legal holds are supported via a hold flag — held data is retained and excluded from automated deletion.
- Redaction & pseudonymization: we support on-export redaction rules (field-level redaction using deterministic pseudonymization) or delivery of raw exports with a redaction map. Redaction does not remove the fact that an event occurred; we preserve event-level metadata (timestamp, actor id hash, operation) to maintain audit fidelity.
- Delivery options: cross-account S3 (recommended) with server-side encryption, presigned URLs, direct SFTP to a customer-managed endpoint, or physical encrypted media (by SOW; chain-of-custody procedure documented).
- Integrity/verification: every export bundle includes manifest.ndjson and manifest.sig. Customers can verify file checksums and manifest signature. Optionally, we will provide a signed acceptance receipt after the transfer completes.

Filename convention example: redwood_audit.v2.{table_name}.YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ.{part}.ndjson.gz

Open question for Legal: please confirm fields that you require redacted in delivery (PII examples: full PAN, unmasked SSN, cardholder_name). If you provide a redaction spec we’ll scope redaction costs; default export is raw with an accompanying redaction map.

Happy to present this on the 10/05 call; I can prepare an extended appendix with sample NDJSON rows and a sample Merkle anchor if you need cryptographic proofs included in the RFP.

— Laura
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
